# How to contribute to Stan?

::: {.callout-important}
You [don't]{.hl} need to be a professional software developer or statistician in order to contribute to Stan!
::: 

## Types of contributions
There are many ways to contribute to Stan, including:

- [asking and answering questions](#sec-participate-in-stan-discourse) on [Stan Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org)
- [reporting problems](#sec-issues-bug-report) when interacting with the software or documentation
- [requesting new features](#sec-issues-feature-request) or improvements
- providing [feedback on documentation](#sec-feedback-on-documentation)
- contributing with a [case study](#sec-contributing-tutorial) of your specific research field
- contributing [code](#sec-contributing-code)

---

## Typical workflows for contributing

### Participate in the Stan Discourse {#sec-participate-in-stan-discourse}

- [Stan Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org) is the main forum for users and
developers to ask questions, discuss issues, and share ideas.
- we want a friendly and welcoming environment
  + [Code of Conduct](https://mc-stan.org/code-of-conduct.html)
  + [Discourse guidelines](https://discourse.mc-stan.org/guidelines)

---

### Feature requests and bug reports {#sec-feature-requests-and-bug-reports}

- go to the GitHub repository ![](img/github_logo.png){width="3%"} of interest
- get familiar with Issues and PRs ([Example: loo](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/issues))
- for [new contributors]{.hl}
  + check for labels like "help wanted" or "good first issue"
  + avoid working on issues that incorporate refactoring or larger changes
  + when in doubt, ask in the issue whether it's a good idea to work on it
- open a [new Issue]{.hl}
  + check first whether the issue already exists (avoid duplicates)
  + some tips for writing good Issues...

---

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing good Issues: Bug Report {#sec-issues-bug-report}

+ Title: One sentence, specific, searchable.
+ Body
  + What happened vs what you expected
  + Minimal reproducible example (i.e., small model/script/data that triggers the problem)
  + (Optional) Environment: OS, hardware if relevant
  + Exact steps to reproduce the problem.
  + Logs / error output (if possible as text in a code block, not a screenshot, so it's searchable)

+ Examples: 
  + [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/425)
  + [brms](https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/1899)
:::

---

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing good Issues: Feature Request {#sec-issues-feature-request}

+ Title: One sentence, specific, searchable.
+ Body
  + describe the problem or limitation
  + (optional) propose solution
  + (optional) note scope of Issue: small, self-contained or does it open a design discussion?

+ Examples:
  + [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/73)
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Additional references:**

+ [Mozilla's guide](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/page.cgi?id=bug-writing.html) to writing good bug reports
+ ["How to Report Bugs Effectively"](https://www.chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/bugs.html) by Simon Tatham
+ R package ["reprex" (tidyverse)](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/): runs your code, captures output, and formats it (code + results) as ready-to-paste Markdown for GitHub issues

:::

---

### Feedback on documentation {#sec-feedback-on-documentation}

- clarifying confusing sections
- adding examples/code snippets
- fixing inaccuracies (e.g., when current behavior deviates from the documented behavior)
- let us know if something is missing or unclear
- fixing typos, grammar, broken links

---

### Contributing a case study or tutorial {#sec-contributing-tutorial}

- list of [case studies in Stan](https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/case-studies.html)
- blog post by Bob Carpenter on [expanding the Stan Users Guide](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2026/05/04/expanding-the-stan-users-guide/)

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-note}

## Checklist for contributing a case study 

::: {.fragment}
**1. Initial contact**

  + post on the [Stan Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org) to reach the team
  + post case study or tutorial idea in the [Stan Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org) first
:::

::: {.fragment}
**2. Content requirements**

  + write it as a narrative document, not just code
  + use a reproducible-notebook format
  + note exact software and compiler versions used
  + fix random seeds so results are exactly reproducible
:::

:::
:::

---

::: {.callout-note}

## Checklist for contributing a case study (continued)
::: {.fragment}
**3. Licensing**

  + license code under an open source license (e.g., BSD or GPL)
  + license text as Creative Commons (CC-BY is most common)
  + author retains copyright (but Stan needs to be permitted to host and redistribute)
:::

::: {.fragment}
**4. Metadata for published case study**

  + Title
  + Author(s) (and optional affiliation)
  + Short abstract/description (in 2-4 sentences, what problem is solved and why it matters)
  + Keywords (3-6 terms for discoverability)
  + Source repository link (e.g., a public GitHub repo containing the actual notebook/knitr source, separate from the rendered HTML)
  + Dependencies list (package/library versions used)
  + Rendered HTML version (the actual output others will read)

:::
:::

---

### Contributing Code {#sec-contributing-code}

Some packages have templates others don't, but overall a good PR description should incorporate the following information:

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-note}
## Writing a good PR description
::: {.fragment}
**Before you start:**

+ Have you read the contributing guidelines? (see GitHub repository)
+ Have you read the [AI Contribution Policy](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/AI-Contribution-Policy)?
+ For contributing to Stan core libraries (e.g. `stan`, `math`, `stanc3`):
  + Have you checked the [Developer Wiki](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki)?
+ Keep the PR small and focused on one logical change
+ Not ready for review yet? Open it as a **Draft PR** so reviewers know to hold off.

:::

::: {.fragment}
**Title:** One sentence, specific, searchable.

+ Good: `Fix incorrect ESS calculation for thinned chains`
+ Avoid: `Bug fix`

:::
:::
:::

---

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing a good PR description (continued I)
::: {.fragment}
**Body:**

+ Link PR to Issue via [GitHub keywords](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue-using-a-keyword) like `Fixes #123` or `Closes #123`
:::
::: {.fragment}
*Description*

+ Describe what has been changed and why.
+ Be concise and use your own words (try to avoid using AI-generated text).
+ Add any uncertainties or open questions you have here as well.
:::
::: {.fragment}
*Breaking changes*: Does this PR change existing behavior, APIs, or output? If yes, describe the impact.
:::
::: {.fragment}
*Tests*: (if applicable) Which tests have you added?
:::
::: {.fragment}
*Documentation / Vignettes*: (if applicable) Have you added documentation?
:::
:::

---

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing a good PR description (continued II)
::: {.fragment}
*Checklist*

+ style is consistent with existing code/docs
+ documentation/vignette is rendered locally
+ tests and `devtools::check()` pass
+ AI-assisted development: Disclose if you used an AI assistant and commit that you reviewed the changes critically.
+ `NEWS.md` entry added
+ see our detailed [checklist](#sec-checklist)
:::
::: {.fragment}
*TODOs*: List any remaining tasks you need to complete before the PR is ready to be merged.
:::
::: {.fragment}
**Examples:**

+ [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/425)
+ [brms](https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/1899)

:::
:::

---

### Some reflections on the use of AI-assisted development

+ [Stan AI Contribution Guideline](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/AI-Contribution-Policy)
+ Use your own words when writing the PR description and comments in a PR review process
+ Review all changes made by an AI assistant critically and ask yourself:
  - Is this change correct? Do I need this change? Is this change in the scope of the PR?
+ When in doubt about something, ask rather the Stan developers than the AI assistant
